correctness.rationale: For nonzero bihomogeneous F of bidegree (m,m), restrictions F(tv)=|t|^(2m)F(v) and subharmonicity prove F>=0 and identify harmonic-line directions with zeros. The Euler/Hessian Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, valid also across zero sets by D'Angelo 2000 Theorem 1, gives global psh of log F. Choose affine chart whose infinity F-positive. u(w)=0.5 log F(1,w) is subharmonic with growth at most m log|w|+O(1), hence Riesz mass <=m by Jensen. Nonnegative C2 vanishing at each zero forces f(w)<=C|w-w0|^2 and an atom >=1. Thus at most m zeros; at equality all mass is m simple atoms and the remainder is a bounded entire harmonic function, hence constant. Homogenization yields F=c|L1...Lm|^2. Examples |product of distinct linear forms|^2 attain m. The critical global log-psh theorem was checked in the actual D'Angelo preprint, page 7, including treatment of zeros.
